case_name: Satyajit Ballulbhai Desai and others v State of Gujarat
respondent:
State of Gujarat
Supreme Court of India

20 July 2012
Cr.A. No. 1158/2012 (Arising out of S.L.P. (Cr.) No. 7821/2011)
The Judgment was delivered by : Gyan Sudha Misra, J.
1. Leave granted.
2. The appellants herein have assailed the judgment and order of the High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad dated 29.09.2011 passed in Special Crl. facts: A lady named Surjaben filed a criminal complaint against the appellants alleging that her husband's name was entered in the revenue record without her knowledge.
The complainant obtained a copy of the revenue record and found that one Satyajitbhai Ballubhai Desai forged and created a bogus power of attorney.
The learned Magistrate sent the matter for investigation to the police which registered it as Talod M.Case No.1/2004.

A compromise came to be arrived at between the appellant No.1 Satyajit Ballubhai Desai and the complainant Surjaben wherein the parties agreed that the criminal complaint filed by the complainant will be withdrawn unconditionally.
The complainant as also the appellant No.1 appeared before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Valod and prayed to withdraw the criminal complaint.

A third person and a stranger to the dispute namely Randhirsing Deepsing Parmar felt aggrieved with the order dated February 15, 2005 passed by the JMFC and filed a Special Criminal Application No.918/2007 before the High Court challenging the order of JMFC.
issues: Whether the grant of police remand is an exception or the rule?
Whether the investigating agency must make out a strong case for taking police custody of the appellants?
petitioner_arguments: The grant of police remand should be an exception and not a rule.
The investigating agency must make out a strong case for taking police custody of the appellants.
The appellants have never tried to scuttle the investigation justifying police remand.
respondent_arguments: The order granting police remand is based on valid or justifiable reason on the part of the investigating agency.
The grant of police remand is necessary for conducting further investigation in the case.
court_reasoning: The scheme of S.167 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 is unambiguous in this regard and is intended to protect the accused from the methods which may be adopted by some overzealous and unscrupulous police officers.
The Legislature also noticed this and has therefore permitted limited police custody.
It is the magistrate who has to judicially scrutinise circumstances and if satisfied can order detention of the accused in police custody.
holding: The grant of police remand should be an exception and not a rule, and the investigating agency must make out a strong case for taking police custody of the appellants.
The court upheld the order passed by the magistrate permitting police remand of the appellants for a period of three days.
